subject: Cloud Computing
title: Service Mesh and Zero Trust
description: A quick win: understand Service Mesh and Zero Trust.

hook.text: In microservices, every service talks to dozens of others. A service mesh ensures every conversation is secured.

buildup.text: Service meshes like Istio and Linkerd add encryption, authentication, and observability to service-to-service traffic.

discovery.text: Zero trust networking assumes no connection is safe — even inside your own network. Every request is verified.

twist.text: Traditional firewalls protect the perimeter. In the cloud there is no perimeter. Security must be embedded everywhere.

climax.text: Service meshes and zero trust are converging into the default cloud-native security model. Verify everything.

punchline.text: No perimeter in the cloud. Trust nothing. Verify everything.

quiz.question: Why is zero trust important in cloud-native environments?
options: There is no traditional network perimeter to protect, so every request must be verified
Cloud environments are inherently trustworthy and need no security
Zero trust eliminates the need for encryption entirely

details.summary: Service meshes like Istio enforce zero-trust networking by requiring every service-to-service communication to be authenticated, authorized, and encrypted. This replaces the traditional perimeter security model where internal network traffic was implicitly trusted.
details.whyItMatters: Zero trust is becoming the default security model for cloud-native applications. Service meshes implement it transparently, securing communications without changing application code.
takeaways: Service meshes enforce mutual TLS between all services
Zero trust assumes no network traffic is inherently safe
Policy enforcement happens transparently at the infrastructure layer

faq.question: What is a service mesh?
faq.answer: A service mesh is an infrastructure layer that handles service-to-service communication in microservices architectures. Sidecar proxies attached to each service manage load balancing, encryption, authentication, and observability without changes to application code.

faq.question: Why is zero trust important for cloud?
faq.answer: Cloud environments have no clear network perimeter to defend. Resources are distributed across regions, accounts, and providers. Zero trust verifies every request regardless of origin, preventing lateral movement by attackers who breach any single service.
